items.text: Here is where that gap tends to show up.
If your resume itself needs work, see resume tips for freshers in India .
Think of standing out as climbing three proofs, not chasing one big idea.
One or two projects you can point to and explain, not describe from memory.
A short written case note, a project README, or a two-minute walkthrough video does this.
Open-source contribution has a reputation for being intimidating, reserved for people who already write excellent code.
GitHub reported more than 1.1 billion contributions to public repositories in 2025 alone, a record year, and March 2025 saw the highest single-month count of first-time contributors ever recorded.
A library, framework, or app you use for college work or a personal project gives you a head start, because you already understand the context before you touch the code or docs.
Show it gets you noticed once someone actually looks at your application.

A short informational interview - "I am building X skill and would value 15 minutes to hear how you approached your first year in this role" - gets answered far more often than a direct ask for a referral or a job.

A message that works has three parts: one specific observation about the person's work or company, one relevant proof point of yours (a project link, not just "I am interested"), and one small, easy-to-answer question.

blocks.heading: Standing Out Inside the Interview Room Itself

items.text: Proof and a narrative get you into the room.
Have your project, README, or contribution link ready to pull up on screen or send immediately after the call.
When asked to explain a project, most freshers describe what the technology does.

blocks.heading: Differentiation Mistakes That Quietly Cost Freshers Interviews

items.text: A stack of course-completion certificates signals that you started things.
What made it yours were the choices you made along the way: why you picked that dataset, what approach failed first, what you changed.
Chasing a "unique personal brand" or a quirky opening line in a cover letter usually reads as try-hard, not memorable.
Positioning and proof come first, but they still need a document and a profile to live in once they exist.
For the profile-specific mechanics - headline, about section, and using Open to Work without looking desperate - see LinkedIn profile tips for freshers in India .

The Career & Skills Compass and the portfolio and proof-of-work resources can help you pick a small, realistic first project instead of staring at a blank page - one that genuinely starts building a high-income skill portfolio, not just fills space on a resume.

blocks.heading: One Project Count for More Than Ten

items.text: A tutorial project followed step by step, with no changes or decisions of your own.
An unfinished repository with no README, no live link, and no way for someone else to see it working.
A project description that names the topic ("built an e-commerce site") but not the problem, the tools, or the outcome.
Could this exact sentence be said, word for word, by five other applicants in your batch.
Does it name a specific decision, constraint, or result, rather than a feeling or aspiration.
Can you back it up with one piece of proof - a project, a contribution, a written note - if someone asks "tell me more".
